# Software Design Document: the job-search project

*Generated by Claude Code following the Gru prompt in silent mode (`/g1 silent`) on 2026-10-07. No intake questions, no phase gates, no pushback layer. Compiled from the project's own files, which were read for this document; every field the files could not supply is marked `[TODO: DATA SOURCE]`, `[TODO: DEFINE]`, `[TODO: DEV]` or `[TODO: APPROVE]` rather than invented. Professor Bear has not reviewed it. The Gru prompt was pasted by Professor Bear; this is a run of it by Claude Code, not his answers to Gru's questions.*

## Executive summary

**What this is.** The design document for everything that is being built under the job-search project: a collector that reads company job boards, the filters and audits that say what its output is worth, a ranking of which companies want teaching work done, the shared-code rule that keeps three course folders consistent, the public work that fills the gaps the search found, and the film series that documents all of it.

**Why it exists.** One question runs through three courses: how does a working professor find, and prepare for, advocate, educator and teaching-materials work at AI and design-tool companies, and how does anyone know the answer the tool gives is right? Computational Skepticism asks whether the output is right. Prompt Engineering asks how to work with the AI that produced it, which is conducting it. Branding and AI asks how to present the result so it is understood.

**Where it stands (2026-10-07).** The collector is built and has run once, by hand, on 2026-09-26: 18 boards, 3,446 postings, 97 kept. Nothing runs on a schedule. Five companies the project cares about cannot be read by the tool. The design document written before the build (Lectern's, 2026-09-26) describes a seen-id state file and a quality-report writer that the code does not contain; section 17 lists every difference found. The public gap-filling series has 36 published films and no written chapters.

**What this document does not do.** It does not apply for anything, contact anyone, or score anyone's fit. It documents a system whose last step is always a person deciding.

**Who must decide next.** Professor Bear: whether the collector runs on a schedule; what to do about the five unreadable companies; whether the design document's missing features are built or struck. Section 16 lists these.

## 2. One-page problem summary

**V0 sentence.** The job-search project is a human-supervised toolchain inserted between public company hiring pages and Professor Bear's own decisions about whom to talk to and what to build, that produces dated, checkable evidence (postings kept and rejected with reasons, companies ranked by demand) and public work that fills the gaps that evidence names.

**Ecosystem.** Three applicant-tracking systems publish company job boards as public APIs. Professor Bear teaches three courses in which the same tool is built live.

**Existing components it touches.** The Reallocation Engine (recipes, ATS providers, the `greenhouse-watch` skill), the three course repositories on GitHub, the course process log (`FRICTIONAL.md`), the Brutalist film toolkit, and the YouTube channel.

**Problem summary.** This system is a collector, a set of audits, and a public portfolio for a working professor looking for teaching-materials and advocacy work, that solves *the openings are public but scattered across many boards in three systems, the filter's output looks right whether or not it is, and the gaps in the professor's own record are invisible until the search names them*, through *a stored, re-runnable collector whose every verdict can be checked against the saved response, plus audits that look for what the filter got wrong, plus public work built against the gaps*. It occupies the space between a job-alert email and a hand-built spreadsheet, and it succeeds when Professor Bear can answer "why is this posting on the list, and what did we throw away?" from files, without re-reading the code.

**The single biggest unresolved question.** Whether the 97 kept postings are the right ones. The title audit found 23 false positives and one candidate miss among them, 555 postings sit in families that need a person's judgment, and the random sample of rejects has not been read. The measure of the filter is therefore a measure of its rules, not of its accuracy.

## 3. Architecture principles

### P1: Source words are sacred
**Commitment.** A kept record carries the source's own field names and values untouched, under `original`. Anything the tool works out lives under keys of its own.
**Honors it.** `jobs-of-interest-<date>.json` holds `matched` (the tool's) next to `original` (the source's).
**Violates it.** A unified schema that renames `absolute_url` and `first_published` and keeps only the rename.
**Failure state if ignored.** A reader cannot check a row against the live posting, and a normalization bug becomes indistinguishable from a company's own data.

### P2: Raw response first
**Commitment.** The API response is written to `raw/` before anything parses it.
**Honors it.** `collect.py` calls `write_json(path, payload)` immediately after `fetch_board`.
**Violates it.** Streaming the response into the filter and keeping only what matched.
**Failure state if ignored.** No filter change can be re-run against yesterday, and no verdict can be re-derived.

### P3: The filter is a document
**Commitment.** The rules live in `keywords.json` and `title_families.json`; every kept record says which words matched and why it was kept.
**Honors it.** `matched.kept_because` reads, for example, "role word in title".
**Violates it.** A relevance score whose inputs are not in the output.
**Failure state if ignored.** "Relevant" becomes an assertion, and disagreements have nowhere to go but the code.

### P4: A partial failure is a partial result
**Commitment.** One source failing does not stop the others; every source is reported ok, unavailable or skipped; exit code 3 only when every source failed.
**Honors it.** The `except Exception` around each board in `main()` records `unavailable` and continues.
**Violates it.** Aborting the run on the first timeout.
**Failure state if ignored.** A flaky third-party API makes the tool useless.

### P5: Watch the company, not the current opening
**Commitment.** A company stays on the watch list with zero matches. Professor Bear, 2026-09-26: a company will create the role if it does not have it yet. Employment type and location are context, never a filter.
**Honors it.** Miro, Airtable, Twilio, Netlify and Jasper AI stay in `sources.json` with no signal.
**Violates it.** Pruning the list to the companies that match today.
**Failure state if ignored.** The watcher becomes a snapshot.

### P6: One master for shared code; class writing is never copied
**Commitment.** Shared files are edited in the Computational Skepticism instructor folder and copied out by `lectern/sync.sh`. Logs, READMEs, `CLAUDE.md`, assignment folders and dated run outputs are never copied between classes.
**Honors it.** `sync.sh --check` reports drift and changes nothing.
**Violates it.** Editing the Branding copy of `collect.py` during class and not telling the master.
**Failure state if ignored.** Three copies drift, and a student reading one gets a filter that no longer matches the others.

### P7: The last step is a person
**Commitment.** Nothing in the system applies, emails, or posts on anyone's behalf. Every report ends at a human gate.
**Honors it.** `greenhouse-watch` "ends at the human gate: the report is a list; the person decides."
**Violates it.** An agent step that sends an application when a match crosses a threshold.
**Failure state if ignored.** A matching error becomes an action in the world.

### P8: A number is a pointer to a file
**Commitment.** Every count in a report, a log or a film names the file it came from. A polished summary never stands alone.
**Honors it.** The status report's appendix names where each detail lives; each film's `FACTCHECK.md` lists a source for every row.
**Violates it.** Quoting "97 kept" with no run file behind it.
**Failure state if ignored.** Fluent, confident, unchecked output, which is the failure the project exists to teach about.

### P9: Doubt is recorded where it happened
**Commitment.** Each substantive change, failure and decision is logged in the course process log the same day, in the person's own words, with what the AI did and what the human decided kept apart.
**Honors it.** `FRICTIONAL.md` in each instructor folder; every push adds a row.
**Violates it.** Fixing a bug and not logging that it was found.
**Failure state if ignored.** The record that shows learning, rather than only an artifact, does not exist.

**Principle collision test.** P1 (keep the source's field names) collides with the CSV deliverable, which needs one header row across three sources. **Resolution: P1 is primary for the JSON, the evidence file; the CSV is a derived view.** P5 (watch every company) collides with P9's effort budget: a longer list is more to check. **Resolution: P5 is primary; the list stays long and the cost is accepted.** P6 (never copy class writing) collides with Professor Bear's instruction on 2026-10-07 to add this document to all three folders. **Resolution: this document is treated as shared and is added to the sync list; it is not a class assignment.**

## 4. Core user flows and system interaction map

### Primary flow (a collection run, by hand)

1. **Person runs** `python3 collect.py` in a class folder → **collector reads** `sources.json` and `keywords.json`.
2. **Collector requests** each board from its applicant-tracking API → **API returns JSON** → **state:** one dated file per board in `raw/`.
3. **Collector normalizes** each response to one view per posting → **state:** in memory.
4. **Collector judges** each posting against `keywords.json` → **state:** kept with `matched`, or rejected with a reason.
5. **Collector deduplicates and validates** (title, URL, parseable date) → **state:** the kept set and the reject counts.
6. **Collector writes** `all-jobs-<date>.{json,csv}` and `jobs-of-interest-<date>.{json,csv}`.
7. **Person runs the audits** (`audit_titles.py`, `audit_rejects.py`, `demand_report.py`) → **state:** Markdown reports with blank Verdict columns where a person must judge.
8. **Person reads the reports and decides** whom to talk to, what to build, and whether the filter is wrong. The system's involvement ends.

### Integration flow (system to system)

| System | Protocol | Data exchanged | Who owns the failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Greenhouse boards API | HTTPS GET, JSON, no auth | One call per company, full ad text | Collector: logs unavailable, continues |
| Ashby posting API | HTTPS GET, JSON, no auth | One call per board | Same |
| SmartRecruiters postings API | HTTPS GET, JSON, no auth | Paged listing without ad text, then one detail call per posting (skippable with `--no-detail`) | Same |
| GitHub | `git` over HTTPS, already authenticated on the machine | Each instructor folder, pushed by hand | Professor Bear, with the folder's own `CLAUDE.md` setting who may push |
| YouTube Data API | HTTPS, OAuth | Uploads and playlists, from the staging folder only | The publisher script; the daily quota is 100 uploads |
| Figma (MCP server) | MCP over the Education account | Reads and writes on design files for the Figma series | The person who runs the session; rate limits per day and credits per month apply |
| Claude Code | Local CLI sessions | Builds, audits, drafts | Professor Bear reviews; see P7 and P9 |

### Administrative flow

- **Add a company:** add one row to `sources.json`. No code change.
- **Change the filter:** edit `keywords.json` or `title_families.json`, then `--from-raw` re-filters saved responses with no network.
- **Propagate a shared change:** edit in the master, run `./lectern/sync.sh --check`, then `./lectern/sync.sh`, then commit each repository by hand with its own log entry. The script never commits and never deletes.
- **Record a change:** a log entry in the matching `FRICTIONAL.md`, and a row in its push table when pushed.

**Flow honesty test.** Built as a command-line prototype with no scheduling and no interface, does it solve the stated problem? For finding the list, yes: it already has. For the day-over-day question ("what is new since last time?") no: the collector as built has no state to diff against (section 17, item 1).

## 5. User and business needs

| # | Need | Component that serves it | Pass/fail test |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | The searcher must be able to see every teaching-related posting across all watched companies from one command, without opening a careers page. | C1 Collector, C2 Filter | One run writes a file with every kept posting from every board in `sources.json`. |
| N2 | The searcher must be able to see only what changed since the last run, without re-reading yesterday's list. | **Not built** (C14 planned) | Two runs on unchanged boards report zero new. Currently untestable: no state exists. |
| N3 | The searcher must be able to tell why any posting is on the list, without reading the code. | `matched` and `kept_because` | Every kept record names its matched words and the rule that kept it. |
| N4 | The searcher must be able to re-derive the list from saved responses after changing the filter, without re-fetching. | `raw/` and `--from-raw` | Re-running over one day's `raw/` reproduces that day's outputs. |
| N5 | The searcher must be able to know what the filter threw away, not only what it kept. | C4 Title audit, C5 Reject sample | A report lists rejects by reason, the disagreements between filter and title family, and a seeded random sample with a blank Verdict column. |
| N6 | The searcher must be able to tell which companies want this work done, whether or not they have a matching opening today. | C6 Demand report | A ranking of companies by five kinds of evidence, with location and employment type shown as context only. |
| N7 | The searcher must be able to add a company without editing code. | `sources.json` | Adding a row and re-running includes that board. |
| N8 | Three instructors' folders must be able to carry the same collector without drifting, without copying class writing. | C8 Sync | `sync.sh --check` reports "All three in sync" for every file on its list. |
| N9 | **Business need.** The work must produce public, checkable evidence against the gaps the search found. | C11 Figma series, C12 films | Published films and repositories a reviewer can open. |
| N10 | **Business need.** A student must be able to see the same process the instructor asks of them. | C10 Process log | Each folder's `FRICTIONAL.md` is public and current. |

**Component filter.** Every component in section 6 serves at least one need above. The planned components that serve a need with no current component (N2) are marked planned.

## 6. Core component documentation

Status key: **BUILT** (exists and has run), **BUILT, UNRUN** (exists, never run in anger), **PLANNED** (specified, not built).

### C1: Collector (`lectern/collect.py`), BUILT, run once

**Problem it solves.** Three APIs with three shapes and one needing one call per posting; downstream should be able to assume the responses are on disk.
**How it works.** Reads `sources.json` (three providers: 11 Greenhouse, 6 Ashby, 1 SmartRecruiters board) and `keywords.json`; fetches each board over HTTPS from three allow-listed hosts with redirects refused; writes the raw response; normalizes; judges; drops duplicates and records missing a title, URL or date; writes `all-jobs-<date>` and `jobs-of-interest-<date>` as JSON and CSV. Standard library only. Exit 0 ran, 2 bad input, 3 every source failed.
**Principle alignment.** P1, P2, P3, P4, P5.
**Flow placement.** Steps 1 to 6 of the primary flow.
**Edge cases.** (1) A board returns an empty list: valid, recorded as zero postings. (2) A board name containing a space (Jasper AI): URL-encoded. (3) A same-day second run: raw and output files are named by date, so a second run on the same day overwrites the first. [TODO: DEFINE] whether that is wanted.
**Scope boundary.** Does not rank companies, does not score fit, does not remember what it has seen.

### C2: Filter (`keywords.json` v0.4.0, `judge()` in `collect.py`), BUILT

**Problem it solves.** Turning "jobs about teaching" into a rule a person can apply by hand to one posting.
**How it works.** Keep on any one of three rules: (a) at least one role word in the title (45 role words); (b) at least three topic words in the body when no title match (12 topic words); (c) the body says the job is to make teaching materials for a named audience, requiring both a verb-object phrase and an audience phrase. Per-company ignore lists exist (Writer's). Flexible-terms words (part-time, contract, summer) are recorded and never cause a keep. The file records every word added, measured, cut or rejected, and why.
**Principle alignment.** P3, P5.
**Edge cases.** (1) Boilerplate that matches every posting on one board (Anthropic's footer puts "education" in all 618 postings): the ignore-list mechanism exists; whether to apply it is an open decision. (2) "training" meaning machine-learning training: a named false friend, handled by rejecting that title family. (3) A role word that is recruiting vocabulary (university, campus, student): the audit found these keep recruiters; not yet changed.
**Scope boundary.** Does not rank. Does not read a person's résumé.

### C3: Title families and the title audit (`title_families.json` v0.3.0, `audit_titles.py`), BUILT

**Problem it solves.** There are far fewer job functions than postings. Classifying titles into 20 families (4 keep, 4 judge, 12 reject) turns "read 3,446 postings" into "judge the families, then read the disagreements."
**How it works.** Reports every posting where the filter and its family's expectation disagree. A disagreement is a question: either the filter is wrong or the family rule is wrong.
**Principle alignment.** P3, P8.
**Edge cases.** (1) A title that fits no family: reported as unclassified. [TODO: DEFINE] how many remain. (2) A family rule that is wrong rather than the filter: the report says both can happen. (3) The audit has its own bug history; the log records one found in it.
**Scope boundary.** Judges nothing; it reports.

### C4: Reject sample (`audit_rejects.py`), BUILT, sample not yet read

**Problem it solves.** Missed postings (false negatives) cannot be counted by a script.
**How it works.** Draws a uniform random sample of 100 rejects with a recorded seed, plus the 63 closest calls, with a blank Verdict column. Reading it is the human's step; k misses in the sample implies about k times 34 across all rejects.
**Principle alignment.** P3, P8, P9.
**Edge cases.** (1) The same seed reproduces the same rows. (2) The near-miss tier was 1,013 postings and was narrowed to 63 closest. (3) No verdict is filled in by the script.
**Scope boundary.** Never marks a verdict.

### C5: Demand report (`demand_report.py`), BUILT

**Problem it solves.** A posting is not a slot to fit; it is evidence that a company pays for this work. The unit is the company.
**How it works.** Ranks companies on five kinds of evidence, weakest to strongest: SELLS (an education revenue line), ENABLES (trains its own staff), ADVOCATES (staffs people to teach a public), TEACHES (hires teachers and materials-makers), BUILDS (staffs an education product team). Anthropic shows all five on the 2026-09-26 run.
**Principle alignment.** P5, P8.
**Edge cases.** (1) A company that cannot be read (five of them) is absent from the ranking by construction, not by evidence. (2) Location and employment type are shown, never filtered. (3) Four or five kinds of evidence mean an education business, not a vacancy.
**Scope boundary.** Ranks companies; judges no person's fit.

### C6: Watch list and ATS table (`sources.json`, `ATS.md`), BUILT

**Problem it solves.** Which companies are watched, why, and which cannot be read.
**How it works.** 18 readable boards with the reason each is watched and a tier; five unreadable Tier 1 companies (Google, Adobe, Salesforce, GitHub, Shopify) each flagged `TODO: DATA SOURCE` with the slugs tried. `ATS.md` records which system each company uses and an honest "unknown" where it was not verified.
**Edge cases.** (1) A company's ATS changes. [TODO: DATA SOURCE] no check exists. (2) Counts inside `ATS.md` disagree with each other (the status report found "Greenhouse 12, Ashby 5" and "nine companies"). (3) Google was checked by hand on 2026-09-26 and found to have education roles and a learning organization not visible from outside.
**Scope boundary.** Records; does not discover.

### C7: Sync (`lectern/sync.sh`, `SYNC.md`), BUILT, run for real once

**Problem it solves.** Three copies of one tool drift.
**How it works.** Copies the files in its `SHARED` list from the master to the other two class folders; `--check` reports drift; never deletes, never commits, never touches the not-shared list.
**Edge cases.** (1) A file added to `lectern/` and not to the list is not shared. This happened: `demand_report.py` was missing from Prompt Engineering until 2026-10-07. (2) The master started out behind Branding on 2026-09-26. (3) A shared file edited in the wrong repository: `SYNC.md` gives the recovery steps.
**Scope boundary.** Compares only the files on its list. A file not on the list can differ and the check will say all three are in sync.

### C8: Facts file (`facts/professor-bear-cv.json`), BUILT, partly attested

**Problem it solves.** A résumé as structured facts a matcher can read, without the full résumé ever being committed.
**How it works.** Sections for person, education, experience, awards, publications, sponsored research, teaching, leadership in AI education and teaching philosophy. Attested by Professor Bear on 2026-09-23; two sections added on 2026-09-27 await his review, and any edit resets `attested` to false.
**Edge cases.** (1) Edits reset attestation. (2) The private résumé stays under `private/` and is never committed. (3) No contact details or profile links belong in the public file.
**Scope boundary.** Facts only; no scoring.

### C9: The engine and its watcher (`the-reallocation-engine-fresh/`: recipes, `scripts/ats/`, the `greenhouse-watch` skill), BUILT

**Problem it solves.** Student-facing recipes that say which data to check, which scripts to run, what to log, with an honesty rule about what ran.
**How it works.** Five runnable recipes (gate-behavior, gate-harness, local-wage-adjustment, skill-demand-monitor on samples; workday-connector live); the rest are drafts. `greenhouse-watch` watches one board, diffs it against a state file by job id (first run is a baseline that reports nothing), matches new postings to a JSON résumé by a documented scheme, and stops at the human gate. A case recipe for this search is drafted and not pushed.
**Edge cases.** (1) Its state diff exists for one board, not for Lectern's 18. (2) A recipe marked more finished than its evidence: the lifecycle fields exist to prevent it. (3) The repository's own status file is stale (2026-06-14).
**Scope boundary.** Never applies, never emails.

### C10: Course folders and the process log, BUILT

Three instructor folders, one per class, each with its own `FRICTIONAL.md`, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Each folder's `CLAUDE.md` sets what must be logged, who may push and what must stay out of public files (no absolute local paths, no other people's names, no contact details). The log is a record of what was tried, what went wrong, who did what, and what is still not understood.
**Edge cases.** (1) Computational Skepticism's folder needs Professor Bear's word per push; the other two have standing approval. (2) A log entry for work not reviewed by him says so. (3) Gru's session outputs in the skepticism folder are copied verbatim and never edited.

### C11: Figma for Educational AI series, BUILT in part

**Problem it solves.** The search found the CV never mentions Figma, design systems, certification programs or conference talks; the series is public work built against those gaps.
**How it works.** A repository with a 19-module plan, 40 experiments, a capabilities map, and 36 films published to a YouTube playlist (most unlisted; four public). A certification rubric is drafted from the films' experiments and waits for Professor Bear to sign. A second book, *Brutalist Figma + Claude*, has chapters drafted.
**Edge cases.** (1) The films exist; the book chapters and workshops behind them do not. (2) The follow-up to the Education team with the playlist is not logged as sent. (3) Whether a sign-up video was ever made is marked "ask Bear".
**Scope boundary.** It fills gaps in public; it does not claim to close them.

### C12: Film series and pipeline, BUILT

**Problem it solves.** Showing the process as a dated, public record.
**How it works.** The Brutalist toolkit builds narrated films from drawn scenes and real captures, passes frame and type gates, and stages a 4K master into one staging folder; the publisher uploads only from that folder. The series *Professor Bear Does His Assignments* has its own playlist; film 1 is the introduction. A pronunciation dictionary for the narrator was started on 2026-10-07.
**Edge cases.** (1) A tool whose public page blocks capture (Claude's and ChatGPT's front pages) cannot be shown as itself, so it is not shown. (2) A tool renamed under the series (NotebookLM is now Gemini Notebook) makes older notes wrong. (3) Older films are made unlisted, never deleted, because students have commented on some.
**Scope boundary.** Publishing is on Professor Bear's word; public is his manual flip.

### C13: Anthropic-board matcher and n8n workflow, BUILT, in a separate repository

A 2026-10-03 assignment pulled Anthropic's live board (640 postings) through a new `matcher.py` and an n8n workflow, scoring 714 postings in about 3 seconds. It is not in the canonical folders. [TODO: DEFINE] whether it joins the master.

### C14: Seen-id state and day-over-day diff, PLANNED

Specified in the earlier design (N2) and not in the collector. Without it there is no "what is new" answer and no second dated run to compare.

### C15: Scheduler, PLANNED, undecided

Nothing runs automatically. The earlier design marks it out of scope; the only launchd agents on the machine are the film loops, and launchd cannot read the Documents folder without Full Disk Access for the shell.

### C16: Readers for the five unreadable companies, PLANNED, undecided

A browser-driven reader, or a monthly manual check. [TODO: DATA SOURCE] for each company's actual ATS.

### C17: Probe runner (Computational Skepticism Assignment 3), PLANNED

Robustness and explanation: whether a fluent explanation names the feature that actually moves the output. Nothing built.

## 7. External integrations and dependencies

| Integration | Owner | Design reason | Contract | Failure mode and fallback | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Greenhouse boards API | Greenhouse | Full ad text in one call | HTTPS GET, no auth, no documented rate limit, unversioned beyond `/v1`; the slug is not always the company name | Source marked unavailable; others continue | Medium: a public endpoint that can change without notice |
| Ashby posting API | Ashby | One call, full description | HTTPS GET, no auth; board names may contain spaces | Same | Medium |
| SmartRecruiters postings API | SmartRecruiters | The only route to Canva's board | Paged listing with no ad text; one detail call per posting | Listing failure marks the source unavailable; `--no-detail` skips the calls | High: one call per posting is the likeliest to be rate-limited |
| Python 3 standard library | n/a | Nothing to install | `urllib`, `json`, `csv`, `re`, `html` | n/a | Low |
| GitHub | GitHub | Public record of the work | Three repositories, one instructor folder each | A push needs the folder's approval rule | Low |
| YouTube Data API | Google | Publishing the series | 100 uploads a day since the 2026-09-28 review; uploads only from the staging folder | Quota exhaustion stops uploads until the next day | Medium |
| Figma MCP and Education account | Figma | The Figma series | Rate limits per day and credits per month | The series pauses | Medium |
| Brutalist toolkit (Manim, Remotion, a local voice) | Professor Bear | Films with no paid steps | Local render, gates | A failed gate blocks the master | Low |
| n8n | n8n | The Branding assignment's workflow export | Local install | The Python collector runs without it | Low |

**Dependency map and single points of failure.** No board is load-bearing; any one can fail and the run produces a result. The single point of failure is the keyword list: its failure is silent, because a badly tuned filter writes a plausible file with the wrong contents. That is why the audits exist.

## 8. Data architecture and state management

**Entity inventory**

| Entity | Owner | Lifecycle | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw board response | The ATS | Written once per run, dated, never modified; `raw/` is gitignored (44 MB for the one run) | Public |
| All-jobs and jobs-of-interest files | Collector | One dated pair per run | Public |
| Quality, demand, title and reject reports | The person and the audit scripts | Written by hand or script; the one dated quality report is a narrative written outside `collect.py` | Public |
| Keyword list, title families, watch list | The person | Edited by hand, version-controlled, versioned inside the file | Public |
| Facts file | The person | Edited rarely; attestation resets on edit | Public subset only |
| Private résumé, tracker, contacts | The person | Under `private/` and `data/ats/`, gitignored | **Private; never copied, paraphrased or committed** |
| Process log | The person, with Claude Code | Appended per substantive change | Public; no absolute paths, no other people's names |
| Film masters and staging records | The pipeline | Built per film; staged copies in one staging folder | Public once published |

**State management strategy.** The collector is stateless per run: its inputs are the watch list, the keyword file and the network. It has no seen-id file (section 17, item 1). `greenhouse-watch` is the one component with a state file and a first-run baseline. The reasoning for stateless collection is that a dated snapshot avoids reconciling deletions and expiry, and makes history auditable.

**Data flow.** HTTP response → raw file → normalize → judge → deduplicate and validate → write outputs → audits and reports → person.

**Consistency model.** Consistent within a run against the snapshots on disk; stale against the live boards by as long as the interval between runs, which today is "since 2026-09-26". The user-visible consequence, to be stated wherever a number is shown: this is what these boards said at this timestamp.

**Retention, archival and deletion.** Raw responses are kept because they are what makes a verdict re-derivable. [TODO: DEFINE] whether `raw/` is pruned after a term. No personal data from third parties is stored; postings are public. Nothing here falls under a retention rule that has been checked. [TODO: DEFINE] whether any posting text containing a named person needs handling.

## 9. Domain model and entity definitions

**Ubiquitous language**

| Term | Definition | Common misuse to reject |
|---|---|---|
| Posting | One job advertisement as one ATS returned it | Not "job": the same job can be two postings on two boards |
| Source | One ATS provider (Greenhouse, Ashby, SmartRecruiters) | Not one company |
| Board | One company's postings within one source | Not "source" |
| Kept | Passed the filter and the completeness check | Never "a good job" or "relevant" |
| Rejected | Did not match, or lacked a required field; always has a reason | Not "bad job" |
| Matched words | The strings that caused a keep, with the rule that kept it | Not a score; there is no score |
| Original | The source's record, unmodified, inside every kept record | Never a normalized copy |
| Title family | One of 20 classes of job function, each declaring keep, judge or reject | Not a verdict on any one posting |
| Demand evidence | One of five kinds (SELLS, ENABLES, ADVOCATES, TEACHES, BUILDS) that a company pays for teaching work | Not fit |
| Tier | How much the company matters to the search | Not a ranking of the company's quality |
| Recipe | A student-facing operating procedure in the engine | Not a script |
| Gate | A hard stop a person clears | Not a vote |
| Master / copy | The canonical shared file and its propagated copy | A copy is never edited to change the master |
| Frictional entry | A dated log entry in seven fields | Not a summary of success |
| Attested | A facts file the owner has read and signed off | Not "accurate" |

**Entities and invariants**

- **Posting.** `source`, `company`, `source_id`, `title`, `url`, `location_text`, `department`, `date_posted`, `date_raw`, `text`, `original`, `matched`.
  - **INV-1** `(source, source_id)` is unique in an output. *Enforced: application layer.*
  - **INV-2** `title`, `url` and a parseable `date_posted` are present in every kept record. *Enforced: application layer.*
  - **INV-3** `original` is byte-identical to the raw file's record. *Enforced: **neither**. This invariant has no runtime check.*
  - **INV-4** a kept record's `matched` shows the rule that kept it. *Enforced: application layer.*
- **Watch-list entry.** `provider`, `company`, `slug`, `tier`, `why_watched`.
  - **INV-5** every provider is one of three implemented. *Enforced: the allow-listed hosts refuse anything else.*
- **Shared file.** A path on `sync.sh`'s list.
  - **INV-6** every listed file is byte-identical in the three folders. *Enforced: `sync.sh --check`, only for listed files. Files not on the list are enforced nowhere.*
- **Facts file.** 
  - **INV-7** `attested` is true only if the owner has read the current content. *Enforced: by convention in `CLAUDE.md`, not by code.*
- **Film.**
  - **INV-8** a film is uploaded only from the staging folder, after its gates pass. *Enforced: the publisher script and a global rule.*

**Bounded contexts.** Three. **Collection** (boards, postings, raw responses, filters, audits). **Search** (the facts file, the gap analysis, the recipe, the decision). **Teaching** (the course folders, the process logs, the films). Lectern lives in Collection and never reads Search, which is why it cannot score fit and why that is a decision rather than a gap.

---

## 10. API contract documentation

The project exposes no network API. Its contracts are command lines and files.

### Command lines

| Invocation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `python3 collect.py` | Fetch all boards, judge, write four dated output files and raw responses |
| `python3 collect.py --only <provider>` | One provider |
| `python3 collect.py --from-raw <dir>` | No network; re-judge saved responses for today's date |
| `python3 collect.py --no-detail` | Skip SmartRecruiters per-posting detail calls |
| `python3 collect.py --sources <f> --keywords <f> --out <dir>` | Alternate configuration and output location |
| `python3 audit_titles.py --all-jobs <f> --out <f> [--families <f>]` | Classify titles, report disagreements |
| `python3 audit_rejects.py --all-jobs <f> --raw <dir> --out <f> [--n 100] [--seed N]` | Draw the reject sample |
| `python3 demand_report.py --all-jobs <f> --kept <f> --out <f>` | Rank companies |
| `./lectern/sync.sh [--check]` | Propagate or check the shared files |

**Exit codes (collector).** 0 ran; 2 bad input (missing or malformed configuration); 3 every board failed. A run where some boards failed exits 0 and names them in the `sources` block. There is no `--dry-run` and no `--all` flag (section 17).

### Output contract, for the agent

`jobs-of-interest-<date>.json`: `tool`, `generated_at`, `keywords_version`, `sources` (one status per board: ok, unavailable or skipped, with a reason), `counts` (`boards_requested`, `boards_ok`, `postings_fetched`, `postings_unique`, `kept`, `rejected` by reason), `note`, and `records`. Each record carries the source's own record under `original` and the tool's under `matched` (`role_title`, `topic_text`, `flex_text`, `materials`, `kept_because`, `title_only`). `all-jobs-<date>.json` carries the same header and every posting with `kept` and `reject_reason`, ad text omitted for size.

### Output contract, for the human

The CSVs carry a documented common subset and are a derived view; the JSON is the evidence. The dated Markdown reports are written for Professor Bear, with a blank Verdict column wherever only a person can judge. [TODO: REPORT FIELD] the quality report has no script that writes it, so its reader, columns and decision are defined by convention, not by code.

## 11. Data flow and sequence diagrams

**Happy path.** Person → collector: run. Collector → each API: GET board (async per board in order, no concurrency). API → collector: JSON. Collector → disk: raw file. Collector → disk: four output files. Person → audit scripts: run. Audit scripts → disk: reports. Person: reads, judges, decides.

**Failure path 1: a board is down.** Collector → API: GET. API → collector: timeout. Collector: records `unavailable`, continues. Outputs are written from the other boards; the `sources` block names the gap.

**Failure path 2: the filter is wrong.** Person → `audit_rejects.py`: draw a sample. The first sample's construction exposed two problems before it was read: the word `education` in all 618 Anthropic postings (a salary footer), and the topic-word rule keeping recruiters. Person: decides; nothing in `keywords.json` was changed without the decision.

**Failure path 3: a shared file is missing from the sync list.** Person: edits a shared file in the master. `sync.sh --check`: reports "All three in sync" for listed files. A comparison outside the list shows one file absent from a copy. Person: adds it to the list and runs the sync.

**Flags.** No chatty interfaces. The only synchronous calls to an unreliable dependency are the SmartRecruiters detail calls, which is why `--no-detail` exists. There is no acknowledgement path for the person's decision; the log is it.

**Minimum viable system.** C1, C2, C6, C7, C10: one command, a documented filter, a watch list, a sync rule and a log. That is the whole of what has run. It answers "what is on the boards, and why is this one on my list?" It does not answer "what is new?" (C14), and it does not cover the five companies that matter most (C16). It is useful, and it is incomplete in exactly those two ways.

## 13. Out of scope

| Item | Reason | Decided | Reopen condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applying, emailing or contacting anyone | The last step is a person (P7) | 2026-09-26 design; stated in the watcher | Permanently excluded |
| Scoring a person's fit in the collector | The collector lives in Collection and never reads Search | Design | Only inside the engine's own matcher, under a documented scheme |
| Treating employment type or location as a filter | Professor Bear, 2026-09-26: a company will make a role for good enough work | 2026-09-26 | His decision |
| A live database or board mirror | Dated snapshots avoid reconciling deletions and expiry | Design | Only if daily runs begin and a diff proves insufficient |
| Paid generation in the film pipeline | Every step is free | Standing rule | Per beat, on his approval |
| Uploading from anywhere but the staging folder | A global rule | Standing | Permanently excluded |
| Reading private data in any shared file | Public repositories | Standing | Permanently excluded |

**Scope realism check.** One person, working alongside teaching, with an AI doing the typing. The MUST-BUILD items are built except C14. The IMPORTANT items not built (C16, C17, the Figma chapters) are each larger than the built ones. The honest reading is that the build is ahead of the evidence about the build: much exists, and one run supports it.

## 14. Infrastructure and deployment requirements

**Compute and runtime.** One Mac, run by hand. Python 3 standard library for the collector and audits; Node for the engine's scripts; local Manim, Remotion and a local voice for films. [TODO: DEFINE] whether a dedicated second machine for the film loops is in service; an earlier note said one was due around 2026-09-29, and nothing read for this document confirms it arrived.

**Networking.** Outbound HTTPS to three allow-listed hosts for the collector; GitHub; YouTube; Figma.

**Data infrastructure.** Files in folders under version control; `raw/` and private folders gitignored.

**Deployment model.** There is no deployment: the tool is a script. Instructors push folders; students read them.

**Observability.** The `sources` block per run, the dated reports, the process logs. No metrics, no alerting.

**Availability and recovery.** No uptime target. The recovery plan for a lost output is to re-run `--from-raw` over the saved responses, which survive as long as `raw/` does. [TODO: DEFINE] a backup for `raw/`, which is gitignored.

**Scaling.** At 18 boards a run takes minutes, dominated by SmartRecruiters' per-posting calls. At 10 times the boards the likeliest failure is a rate limit. [TODO: DEFINE] a limit and a back-off.

**Scheduling.** None. A daily run needs Full Disk Access for the shell, or a scheduler on another machine.

## 15. Risk register

| # | Risk | Category | Likelihood | Impact | Trigger | Mitigation | Contingency | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The filter keeps the wrong postings and a person trusts the list | Silent failure | High (already found) | High | 97 kept, 23 false positives, 555 undecided | Audits, published matches, the reject sample | Re-judge from `raw/` | Professor Bear |
| R2 | The filter misses the right postings | Silent failure | Unknown | High | The reject sample is unread | Read it and multiply | Add words; log the measurement | Professor Bear |
| R3 | A public endpoint changes or closes | External dependency | Medium | High | Collector reports a board unavailable | Per-source isolation | Add a different reader | Professor Bear |
| R4 | `original` is altered and nothing notices | Data integrity | Low | High | A normalization bug | A test that diffs a record against its raw original [TODO: DEV] | Re-fetch | Professor Bear |
| R5 | The shared copies drift | Process | High (happened) | Medium | A file not on the sync list | Keep the list complete; `--check` | The recovery steps in `SYNC.md` | Professor Bear |
| R6 | The five unreadable companies are the ones that matter most | Coverage | High | High | Google, Adobe, Salesforce, GitHub, Shopify | A reader, or a monthly hand check | Name the gap in every report | Professor Bear |
| R7 | One run is mistaken for a method | Evidence | High | High | Every number comes from 2026-09-26 | A second run | Say "one run" wherever a count appears | Professor Bear |
| R8 | AI-typed answers stand as the owner's | Accountability | Medium | High | The Gru specification session: Claude Code typed his answers and confirmed gates, unreviewed | Review them; label them | Mark them "not reviewed" | Professor Bear |
| R9 | A film overclaims or goes stale | Public record | Medium | Medium | Tools change fast; a tool is renamed | Date every film; re-test | Unlist, never delete | Professor Bear |
| R10 | Private data reaches a public file | Security | Low | High | A résumé or contact detail copied in | The folders' privacy rules; a scan script in the engine | Remove and rewrite history only on his word | Professor Bear |
| R11 | The video quota or an account limit blocks publishing | External | Medium | Low | Daily YouTube or Figma limits | Budget bulk work around them | Wait for the reset | Professor Bear |

**Top three.** **R1 and R2** together: the tool's output looks the same whether the filter is right or wrong, and the number that would settle it, the miss rate, has not been measured. **R6**: the strongest evidence in the demand report is about companies the tool cannot see. **R7 and R8**: one run and unreviewed AI-typed answers are the two places where a polished record can outrun what is actually established.

## 17. As built versus as designed (found while compiling this document)

Each row was checked by reading the current `collect.py` and the earlier design (`assignment-3/SDD.md` in the Branding and AI folder, version 0.1.1).

| # | Earlier design says | The code does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A state file of seen ids per source; the second run reports only what is new; `--dry-run` and `--all` flags; "the state file is never written on a failed run" | `main()` has no state file, no seen-id set, and no `--dry-run` or `--all`. Its flags are `--sources`, `--keywords`, `--out`, `--only`, `--from-raw`, `--no-detail` | `collect.py` argument list and `main()`; the status report also marks a second run as not done |
| 2 | A quality report written with each run | The module's docstring says `quality-report-<date>.md` is written; `main()` writes four files and no report. The dated quality report on file is a narrative that was written outside the collector | `collect.py` writes only `all-jobs` and `jobs-of-interest`; `grep` finds "quality" only in the docstring |
| 3 | Status: "Not built. This document precedes implementation." | The collector is built and has run once | `collect.py`, the run outputs of 2026-09-26 |
| 4 | Keep on a role word in the title or topic words in the body | A third keep rule exists: the body says the job is to make teaching materials for a named audience (keywords v0.4.0) | `judge()` and `keywords.json` |
| 5 | An `all-jobs` file is not described | It exists and carries every posting with its reject reason | `main()` and the run outputs |
| 6 | Three principles about failure and isolation | Implemented as designed: raw response first, per-board isolation, hosts allow-listed, redirects refused | `get()` and `main()` |

**Consequences.** Need N2 (what is new since last time) is unserved by the built tool. A reader who takes the earlier design's description of the collector as the collector's behavior would be wrong in rows 1 and 2.
